assessments.summary: The row-counting argument establishes D(77) <= 154, and the reproduced verifier is conditionally sound: a successful run on the supplied payload would establish a 152-point no-three-in-line configuration in the 76 x 76 grid and hence D(77) >= 152 by inclusion into the 77 x 77 grid. However, the bounded record contains neither trusted successful-execution evidence nor an independently checked exhaustive determinant trace. Thus the decisive noncollinearity predicate, the lower bound D(77) >= 152, and consequently the full interval 152 <= D(77) <= 154 remain unverified.
scopeQualifications: No external dependency is required; the database links are provenance-only because the payload and verifier are reproduced in the subject.
The encoding/cardinality checks establish 152 distinct in-range grid points.
The verifier's determinant test correctly characterizes collinearity and uses exact integer arithmetic.
The upper bound D(77) <= 154 is established because each of the 77 horizontal rows contains at most two points.
A 154-point configuration would have exactly two points in every row and, by the analogous column argument, every column.
evidenceIssues: The quoted successful-verification output is an untrusted assertion rather than objective execution evidence.
No pinned successful execution of the verifier on the supplied configuration is present.
No independently supplied exhaustive trace verifies nonzero determinants for all 573,800 triples.
